questions.question: If \(N\) is an odd integer, which of the following **must** be even?

solution.exhibit_text:
This is a perfect problem for Picking Numbers. Pick a simple number for \(N\), like 3. Then plug it into the answer choices and see which one is correct.

(A) \(2(3)+1=6-1=5\). Eliminate.
(B) \(3(3)+2=9+2=11\). Eliminate.
(C) \(4(3)=12\). Keep.
(D) \((3)^2+2(3)=9+6=15\). Eliminate.

Only (C) works.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is \(208\) inches. The ratio of its length to its width is \(5{:}3\). What are the dimensions of this rectangle?

solution.exhibit_text:
Since you know that the rectangle's perimeter is 208, you can use the ratio of length to width and the perimeter formula to set up a proportion. \(P=2(\ell+w)\), so proportionate to the length and width, the perimeter is \(2(5+3)=16\). Set up a proportion using the length and the perimeter, then cross multiply and divide to solve:

\[\dfrac{5}{16}=\dfrac{\ell}{208}\]
\[16\ell=1{,}040\]
\[\ell=65\]

Note that the lengths and widths in the answer choices are all different, so you only need to find one of them to find the answer. (B) is correct.

questions.question: In the equation \(3y+10=5y-25\), what is the value of \(y\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
To solve the given equation for \(y\), start by adding 25 to both sides, then subtract \(3y\) from both sides. Finally, divide by the coefficient of \(y\).

\[3y+10=5y-25\]
\[3y+35=5y\]
\[35=2y\]
\[17.5=y\]

questions.question: Nick and Alex worked on a paper together. If Nick wrote \(\dfrac{2}{7}\) of the paper and Alex wrote \(20\) pages, then what was the total length of the paper?

solution.exhibit_text:
If Nick wrote \(\dfrac{2}{7}\) of the paper, then Alex must have written the other \(\dfrac{5}{7}\) of the paper. This means \(\dfrac{5}{7}\) of the paper is equal to 20 pages.

\[\dfrac{5}{7}P=20\]

To solve for \(P\), multiply both sides of the equation by the reciprocal of \(\dfrac{5}{7}\), which is \(\dfrac{7}{5}\).

\[P=\dfrac{7}{5}\times20\]
\[P=28\]

The paper is 28 pages long.

questions.question:
A chemist is preparing a solution by combining the contents of several containers:
• Three 1.5-liter flasks
• Five 250-milliliter beakers
• Two 75-milliliter test tubes

If the chemist pours all of these into one large vat, what is the total volume of the solution, in liters?

solution.exhibit_text:
To determine the total volume, add up all of the chemist's containers. Three 1.5 liter flasks give \(3\times1.5\) liters \(=4.5\) liters. Five 250-milliliter beakers total \(5\times250=1{,}250\) milliliters. Since there are 1,000 milliliters in 1 liter, this is equivalent to \(\dfrac{1{,}250}{1{,}000}=1.250\) liters.

So far, \(4.5+1.25=5.75\), but there's one more container to add. Choice (D) is the only larger choice and must be correct.

On test day, choose (D) with confidence and move to the next question. For more practice, use similar logic to evaluate the last container. Two 75-milliliter test tubes are \(2\times75=150\) milliliters, or \(\dfrac{150}{1{,}000}=0.150\) liters. Summing these three components gives \(4.5+1.250+0.150=5.9\) liters.

questions.question: There are 50 cards of varying colors in a stack. The probability of drawing a yellow card is 0.4. If 10 yellow cards are removed from the stack, what is the probability of drawing a yellow card from the remaining stack?

solution.exhibit_text: Recall that \(\text{Probability}=\dfrac{\text{Number of Desired Outcomes}}{\text{Number of Total Outcomes}}\). There are 50 total cards, and the probability of drawing a yellow card is 0.4. If \(y\) represents the number of yellow cards, the probability of drawing a yellow card is \(0.4=\dfrac{y}{50}\). This yields \(y=50\times0.4=20\). Thus, there are 20 yellow cards in the stack. The question asks for the probability of drawing a yellow card after 10 yellow cards are removed. This leaves \(20-10=10\) yellow cards out of a total of \(50-10=40\) remaining cards. The probability is thus \(\dfrac{10}{40}=0.25\).

questions.question:
A certain wind turbine completed 32 full rotations in 5 minutes and generated 324 megajoules of electricity. Assuming that the wind speed and electricity generation rate remain constant, which proportions can be used to determine how many rotations it will take the turbine to generate 1,200 megajoules of electricity?
Select the **three** correct answers.

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(x\) be the number of rotations needed to generate 1,200 megajoules of electricity. The ratio \(\dfrac{324\text{ megajoules}}{32\text{ rotations}}\) reflects the rate of 324 megajoules generated in 32 rotations. Set up a proportion to solve for \(x\), keeping megajoules in the numerators and rotations in the denominators: \(\dfrac{324\text{ megajoules}}{32\text{ rotations}}=\dfrac{1{,}200\text{ megajoules}}{x\text{ rotations}}\). This proportion matches (A). (Note that the detail of 5 minutes was not needed to solve the question.) Evaluate the remaining answer choices by cross multiplying to see which are equivalent to \((324)(x)=(32)(1{,}200)\).

(B): \((32)(1{,}200)=(324)(x)\) is equivalent to \((324)(x)=(32)(1{,}200)\); correct
(C): \((1{,}200)(32)=(324)(x)\) is equivalent to \((324)(x)=(32)(1{,}200)\); correct
(D): \((324)(32)=(x)(1{,}200)\) is not equivalent to \((324)(x)=(32)(1{,}200)\); eliminate
(E): \((1{,}200)(x)=(32)(324)\) is not equivalent to \((324)(x)=(32)(1{,}200)\); eliminate

questions.question: A student is choosing 3 books to read over the summer from a list of 7 different recommended novels. How many different sets of 3 books can the student choose?

solution.exhibit_text:
The student must choose 3 books to read. Since there are 7 available books, there are 7 options for the first book. After the first book has been selected, there are only 6 left to choose from. Similarly, after the second has been selected, there are only 5 left. Therefore, there are \(7\times6\times5=210\) total ways to choose the three books.

However, this method imposes an order on the way the books are chosen. In reality, choosing 3 books from a group of 7 can be done in any order you want. To account for this, you must divide by the total number of ways to arrange 3 books, which is \(3\times2\times1=6\). Therefore, the final result is \(\dfrac{210}{6}=35\).

questions.question: A furniture store buys dining tables for a wholesale cost of \(w\) dollars each. To cover shipping and handling, the manager first increases the purchase cost by 10%. Then, to determine the final selling price, the manager applies an additional 45% markup to that new total. Which expression represents the final selling price of each dining table?

solution.exhibit_text:
To find the expression for the final selling price, you must apply each percentage increase sequentially rather than adding the percentages together. A 10% increase on the wholesale cost \(w\) is \(w+0.1w=1.10w\). Apply the second increase to the new value. A 45% increase on \(1.10w\) is:

\[1.10w+(0.45)(1.10w)=1.10w(1+0.45)\]
\[=1.10w\times1.45\]
\[=(1+0.10)\times1.45w\]
\[=1.45w+0.145w\]
\[=1.595w\]

questions.question:
Two expressions are given:
\(11-x\)
\(-5(1.5x+2)\)

Which of these are equivalent to the difference of these expressions, if the second expression is subtracted from the first expression?
Select the **two** correct answers.

solution.exhibit_text: Set up an expression that subtracts the second expression from the first expression, using parentheses to make sure you don't lose any of the signs: \(11-x-[-5(1.5x+2)]\). Distribute the \(-5\): \(11-x-(-7.5x-10)\). Rewrite the terms that are in parentheses, making sure to distribute the subtraction sign before the parentheses: \(11-x+7.5x+10\). Then combine like terms: \(11+10-x+7.5x=21+6.5x\). This matches (D). (C) is also correct, since it shows the step before adding like terms.

questions.question: A drawer contains 8 black socks and 4 blue socks. If 2 socks are pulled out at random without replacement, what is the probability that they are a matching pair of blue socks?

solution.exhibit_text: Recall that \(\text{Probability}=\dfrac{\text{Number of Desired Outcomes}}{\text{Number of Total Outcomes}}\). There are 4 blue socks and \(8+4=12\) total socks. Therefore, the probability of picking a blue sock on the first pull is \(\dfrac{4}{12}=\dfrac{1}{3}\). After this blue sock has been picked, there are 3 blue socks and 11 total socks remaining. The probability of picking out another blue sock is thus \(\dfrac{3}{11}\). To find the probability of picking out two blue socks, multiply these respective probabilities: \(\dfrac{1}{3}\times\dfrac{3}{11}=\dfrac{1}{11}\).

questions.question: The sum of the numbers \(m\), \(n\), and \(p\) is 24. The ratio of \(m\) to \(n\) is 2:5, and the ratio of \(n\) to \(p\) is 5:3. What is the value of \(n\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
Since the two ratios have \(n\) in common, you can write two equations using the ratios and solve each equation for \(n\). Start by writing the given ratios as fractions:

\[\dfrac{m}{n}=\dfrac{2}{5}\rightarrow m=\dfrac{2}{5}n\]
\[\dfrac{n}{p}=\dfrac{5}{3}\rightarrow p=\dfrac{3}{5}n\]

The question states that \(m+n+p=24\). Substitute in the two equations above and solve for \(n\).

\[m+n+p=24\]
\[\dfrac{2}{5}n+n+\dfrac{3}{5}n=24\]
\[\dfrac{2}{5}n+\dfrac{5}{5}n+\dfrac{3}{5}n=24\]
\[\dfrac{10}{5}n=24\]
\[2n=24\]
\[n=12\]

questions.question: A school debate committee must be formed, consisting of exactly 1 teacher and 2 students. If there are 4 teachers and 6 students available to join the committee, how many different ways are there to form the committee?

solution.exhibit_text: The committee contains exactly 1 teacher. There are 4 possible teachers to choose from, so there are 4 options for this position. The remaining 2 positions must be filled from the 6 available students. There are thus 6 choices for one position. Once this person is assigned, there are only 5 left to choose from. This appears to yield \(6\times5=30\) options for the students. However, this method counts Student A and Student B as a different group than Student B and Student A. In reality, they should be the same because order does not matter in a committee. To correct for this, divide 30 by the number of different ways of arranging 2 students, which is 2. This yields \(30\div2=15\) groups of 2 students. Multiply this by the number of options for the teacher to arrive at the total number of ways of selecting the committee: \(4\times15=60\).

questions.question: If \(\dfrac{x}{y}+\dfrac{3}{x}=\dfrac{\square}{xy}\) and \(x,y\ne0\), what expression is represented by \(\square\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
To add fractions, you need a common denominator. The common denominator of \(x\) and \(y\) is \(xy\). Multiply the first fraction by \(\dfrac{x}{x}\) and the second by \(\dfrac{y}{y}\) to obtain this common denominator. Then add the numerators.

\[\dfrac{x}{y}+\dfrac{3}{x}=\dfrac{\square}{xy}\]
\[\dfrac{x}{y}\left(\dfrac{x}{x}\right)+\dfrac{3}{x}\left(\dfrac{y}{y}\right)=\dfrac{\square}{xy}\]
\[\dfrac{x^2}{xy}+\dfrac{3y}{xy}=\dfrac{\square}{xy}\]
\[\dfrac{x^2+3y}{xy}=\dfrac{\square}{xy}\]

Since the denominator on both sides is the same, \(\square=x^2+3y\).

questions.question: A line whose slope is \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\) passes through the points \((4,2)\) and \((x,1)\). What is the value of \(x\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
The formula for slope is \(\text{Slope}=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}\). Plug in the given information and solve for the missing variable.

\[-\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{1-2}{x-4}\]
\[-\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{-1}{x-4}\]

Since both sides are negative, you can simplify:

\[\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{1}{x-4}\]

Next, cross multiply:

\[x-4=2\]
\[x=6\]

questions.question: Alex is building a large solid cube with an edge length of 4 feet. He constructs it using smaller solid cubes, each with an edge length of 0.5 feet. How many small cubes will Alex need to build the large cube?

solution.exhibit_text: Find how many small cubes fit along one edge by dividing the large cube edge by the small cube edge. First, rewrite 0.5 feet as \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) feet. Then divide 4 feet by \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) feet. Remember that dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, so \(4\div\tfrac{1}{2}=4\times2=8\). This means 8 small cubes stacked in a row make up one edge of the large cube. Since Alex is building a solid cube and the volume of a cube is length × width × height, that number will be: \(8\times8\times8=512\).

questions.question: The CEO of Kool Clothing, Inc. is analyzing the salaries that employees are paid in Kool Clothing stores. The table above shows both the highest salary for each position and the range of salaries for each position. Which of the following expresses the correct **overall** range (\(r\)) of all salaries for all four positions, in thousands?

solution.exhibit_text:
An overall range is the difference between the lowest and highest salaries. Notice that the highest salary according to the table is that of managers, which is 35. Eliminate (A) and (C). To find the lowest salary, subtract the range from each of the highest salaries:

Managers: \(35-5=30\)
Assistant Managers: \(28-4=24\)
Sales Associates: \(23-8=15\)
Cashiers: \(20-3=17\)

The lowest salary among all positions is 15 (Sales Associates). So the overall range of all salaries is \(15\le r\le35\).

questions.question: In James and Sarah's class, extra credit quiz scores range from 0 to 50. Sarah took 6 quizzes, and her mean score was 40. James took 8 quizzes. If both students have the same total score for their quizzes, what was James's mean score?

solution.exhibit_text: Recall that \(\text{Average}=\dfrac{\text{Sum of Values}}{\text{Number of Values}}\). Sarah took 6 quizzes, and her mean was 40, so \(40=\dfrac{\text{Sum of Values}}{6}\). Multiply both sides by 6 to obtain \(240=\text{Sum of Values}\), or total score for the quizzes. James took 8 quizzes, and the sum of his quizzes was the same as Sarah's sum. Therefore, James' average is \(\dfrac{240}{8}=30\).

questions.question: Sally started her summer job making $12 an hour. After three weeks, her wages increased by 20%. Two weeks later, she received an additional 15% increase. What was the total percentage increase in wages that Sally received?

solution.exhibit_text:
The formula for calculating percent increase is \(\text{Percent Change}=\dfrac{\text{Change}}{\text{Original}}\times100\%\). The question gives you the original amount ($12), but you need to calculate Sally's final wage before you can use the formula.

Her first increase was by 20%: \(\$12\times1.20=\$12(1+0.20)=\$12+\$2.40=\$14.40\). The final increase was by 15%, so:

\[\$14.40\times1.15=\$14.40(1+0.10+0.05)\]
\[=\$14.40+\$1.44+\$0.72\]
\[=\$16.56\]

(Note: adding a 1 before the percentage includes the original whole in the new total wage and saves you the need to add the increase to the original amount.)

Next, put the starting and ending wages into the percent change formula:

\[\text{Percent Change}=\dfrac{16.56-12}{12}\times100\%\]
\[=\dfrac{4.56}{12}\times100\%\]
\[=38\%\]

questions.question: The least of a set of 4 consecutive multiples of 3 is \(L\), and the greatest is \(G\). What is the value of \(\dfrac{2G+L}{3}\) in terms of \(G\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
The greatest multiple is \(G\), so the next greatest multiple must be \(G-3\), then \(G-6\), and fourth and last, \(G-9\). Thus, \(G-9\) must be equal to the least value of the set, \(L\). Plug in \(G-9\) for \(L\) in the expression and simplify.

\[\dfrac{2G+L}{3}\]
\[\dfrac{2G+(G-9)}{3}\]
\[\dfrac{3G-9}{3}\]
\[\dfrac{3(G-3)}{3}\]
\[G-3\]

Alternatively, use Picking Numbers to solve. Choose a set of 4 consecutive multiples of 3, such as 3, 6, 9, and 12. Plug in 3 for \(L\) and 12 for \(G\) in the original expression such that \(\dfrac{2(12)+3}{3}=\dfrac{27}{3}=9\). The correct choice will result in 9 when 12 is plugged in for \(G\), and the only choice to do so is (A).

questions.question: Michael drove from point A to point B at 15 miles per hour and immediately returned by the same route at 30 miles per hour. What was his average speed, in miles per hour, for the entire trip?

solution.exhibit_text:
Pick a number for the distance between A and B. To keep the calculations simple, choose a number that both 15 and 30 divide into evenly, such as 60 miles. The total distance then is \(60(2)=120\).

Distance equals rate times time, so you can use \(T=\dfrac{D}{R}\) to find the total time: \(T_1=\dfrac{D}{R_1}\) and \(T_2=\dfrac{D}{R_2}\), \(R_1=15\) mph and \(R_2=30\) mph.

\[T_1+T_2=\dfrac{60}{15}+\dfrac{60}{30}=4+2=6\]

Now, use the average speed formula: \(\text{Average Speed}=\dfrac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Total Time}}\)

Thus, the average speed is \(\dfrac{120}{6}=20\) miles per hour.

questions.question: A man is walking 3 miles per hour toward point B from point A. At the same time, a woman is running 6 miles per hour toward point A from point B. If point A and point B are 15 miles apart, how far from point B will they meet?

solution.exhibit_text:
Try to visualize this problem as two people moving toward each other on a number line. Each hour, these two people move 9 miles closer to each other, so if you divide the total distance of 15 miles by 9, you get the time it takes for them to meet: \(\dfrac{15}{9}=\dfrac{5}{3}=1\tfrac{2}{3}\) hours. To determine the distance from point B, see how far the person beginning at point B travels in that time: \(6\left(1\tfrac{2}{3}\right)=10\) miles.

You could also Backsolve this problem. To do so, choose an answer and determine how long it would take the woman beginning at point B to travel that distance. Then, find how far the man beginning at point A could travel in that same time. If the two distances add up to 15, then the answer is correct.

questions.question: A granola recipe requires \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) of an ounce of vanilla extract. How many batches of granola can be made using a package containing 60 ounces of vanilla extract?

solution.exhibit_text: To answer this question, you have to figure out how many times \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) goes into 60. Since you're dividing by a number smaller than 1, the result must be more than 60, so eliminate (A) and (B). The equation is \(60\div\dfrac{3}{5}=\dfrac{60}{1}\times\dfrac{5}{3}\). Canceling will make the multiplication easier: \(\dfrac{60}{1}\times\dfrac{5}{3}=\dfrac{20}{1}\times\dfrac{5}{1}\), which equals \(20\times5\), or 100.

questions.question:
\[\dfrac{y}{w}=z(w+x)\]
In the equation above, the value of \(w\) is \(-1\) and \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) are greater than 0. What is the value of \(x\) in terms of \(y\) and \(z\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
Plug in \(-1\) for \(w\) and then isolate \(x\). Beware of careless errors with the negatives.

\[\dfrac{y}{-1}=z(-1+x)\]
\[\dfrac{1}{z}(-y)=z(-1+x)\left(\dfrac{1}{z}\right)\]
\[-\dfrac{y}{z}=-1+x\]
\[-\dfrac{y}{z}+1=x\]

Now that \(x\) is isolated, manipulate the expression until you have matched an answer choice:

\[-\dfrac{y}{z}+\dfrac{z}{z}=\dfrac{-y+z}{z}=\dfrac{z-y}{z}\]

questions.question: A commercial printer feeds paper through the rollers at a rate of 10 sheets every 4 seconds. If each sheet is \(x\) inches long, what must \(x\) be in order for the press to process exactly 1,650 inches of paper per minute?

solution.exhibit_text: To find the value of \(x\), first determine how many sheets are processed in one minute. The press moves 10 sheets every 4 seconds. Since there are 60 seconds in a minute, the printer moves \(\dfrac{10\text{ sheets}}{4\text{ seconds}}\times\dfrac{60\text{ seconds}}{1\text{ minute}}=150\dfrac{\text{sheets}}{\text{minute}}\). Next, relate the number of sheets to the total distance per minute. The press must process 1,650 inches per minute. Set up the equation: \(150\dfrac{\text{sheets}}{\text{minute}}\left(x\dfrac{\text{inches}}{\text{sheet}}\right)=1{,}650\dfrac{\text{inches}}{\text{minute}}\), or \(150x=1{,}650\). Divide both sides by 150 to solve for \(x\): \(x=\dfrac{1{,}650}{150}=\dfrac{165}{15}=\dfrac{33}{3}=11\) inches. The length of each sheet must be 11 inches.

questions.question: The sum of two consecutive integers is \(-25\). If 3 is subtracted from the smaller integer and 2 is added to the larger integer, what is the product of the two resulting integers?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(x\) represent the smaller integer. The next consecutive integer is \(x+1\). Their sum is \(-25\).

\[x+(x+1)=-25\]
\[2x+1=-25\]
\[2x=-26\]
\[x=-13\]

The smaller integer is \(-13\), and the larger is \(-13+1=-12\).

Next, subtract 3 from the smaller integer to get \(-13-3=-16\) and add 2 to the larger integer to get \(-12+2=-10\).

Finally, find the product of the two new integers: \((-16)\times(-10)=160\).

questions.question: What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 3 twice in a row on a fair six-sided die, with each of the numbers 1–6 on each side?

solution.exhibit_text: To find the probability of two independent events, find the probability of each individual event and then multiply those probabilities together. Remember that \(\text{Probability}=\dfrac{\text{Number of Desired Outcomes}}{\text{Number of Total Outcomes}}\). You need to find the probability of rolling a 4, 5, or 6 on the die and then multiply that number by itself. In this scenario, there are 3 desired outcomes out of a total of 6, so the probability of rolling a 4, 5, or 6 is \(\dfrac{3}{6}=\dfrac{1}{2}\). Multiply this number by itself to obtain \(\dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{1}{4}\).

questions.question: A committee of 3 people is to be chosen from a group of five 9th graders and four 10th graders. If the committee must consist of two 9th graders and one 10th grader, how many different committees can be formed?

solution.exhibit_text:
There are five 9th graders, and two must be chosen to be part of the committee. There are 5 ways to select the first 9th grader. After he has been chosen, only 4 remain. It appears that there are \(5\times4=20\) selections possible. However, the order in which these 9th graders appear on the committee does not matter. Therefore, you must divide by the number of ways to arrange 2 objects, or \(2\times1\). The final result is \(\dfrac{20}{2\times1}=10\).

There are 4 ways to choose one 10th grader out of a group of four 10th graders.

Each of the 10 ways to choose the 9th graders can be paired with each of the 4 ways to choose the 10th graders. Therefore, a total of \(10\times4=40\) committees are possible.

questions.question: In a sample of 60 ties at a local clothing store, there are 8 purple ties and 32 striped ties. Of the 8 purple ties, 5 have stripes. If a tie is selected at random from the given sample, what is the probability that **both** of the following are true: the tie is **not** purple and does **not** have stripes?

solution.exhibit_text: There's a lot of information in this problem, so break it down piece by piece. In order to find the probability the question asks for, you need to find the number of non-purple unstriped ties. Find the number of purple or striped ties and subtract from 60. \(8\text{ purple}+32\text{ striped}=40\) ties. You might be tempted to go ahead and subtract from 60 now (which would give a probability of \(\dfrac{20}{60}\), or \(\dfrac{1}{3}\)), but remember that 5 ties are *both* purple and striped. You don't want to count those twice, so subtract them: \(40-5=35\). Now you can subtract from 60 to get 25 ties that are neither purple nor striped. The probability of selecting one of these is \(\dfrac{25}{60}\), or \(\dfrac{5}{12}\).

questions.question: Lucia speed walks 3 kilometers in \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) of an hour. At that rate, how many **meters** does she speed walk per minute? (Note: 1 km = 1,000 m)

solution.exhibit_text:
Pay careful attention to the units. You are asked for the rate in meters per minute, so convert kilometers to meters and hours to minutes.

\[3\text{ km}=3\times1{,}000=3{,}000\text{ m}\]
\[\dfrac{2}{3}\text{ hr}=\dfrac{2}{3}\times60=40\text{ minutes}\]

Thus, Lucia speed walks 3,000 meters in 40 minutes, or \(3{,}000\div40=75\) meters per minute.

questions.question: Liz is training on a circular track. She has already run 800 meters. Each lap around the track is exactly 150 meters. If her goal is to run at least 3,400 meters in total, what is the minimum number of full laps she still needs to complete?

solution.exhibit_text:
Liz's goal is to run 3,400 meters, and she has already run 800 meters. Therefore, she has \(3{,}400-800=2{,}600\) meters left. Each lap is exactly 150 meters, so she has \(\dfrac{2{,}600}{150}=\dfrac{260}{15}=\dfrac{52}{3}=17\tfrac{1}{3}\) laps left.

The question asks how many full laps she needs to complete, so round up. 17 is too small; she must run 18.

questions.question: The mean weight of a group of 6 people is 150 pounds. If a 7th person weighing 185 pounds joins the group, what is the new mean weight of the 7 people?

solution.exhibit_text: Recall that \(\text{Average}=\dfrac{\text{Sum of Values}}{\text{Number of Values}}\). If the mean weight of a group of 6 people is 150 pounds, then \(150=\dfrac{\text{Sum}}{6}\). Therefore, \(\text{Sum}=150\times6=900\). To find the new average when the 7th person is included, add the 185 pounds to this sum and divide by 7: \(\dfrac{900+185}{7}=\dfrac{1{,}085}{7}=155\).

questions.question:
\[-2<\dfrac{x}{3}<1\]
Which number line shows the solution to the inequality above?

solution.exhibit_text:
Multiply each term in the equation by 3 to clear the fraction. This will isolate the \(x\).

\[-2(3)<\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)(3)<1(3)\]
\[-6<x<3\]

Since \(x\) is between \(-6\) and 3, choose the number line that is shaded between \(-6\) and 3, with open circles at both endpoints since the inequality is strict, (B).

questions.question: The mean of a set of 10 numbers is 16. Two of the numbers (7 and 13) are removed. What is the mean of the 8 remaining numbers?

solution.exhibit_text:
The mean of a set of values is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. In this question, you already know the mean (16) of the original 10 values, so you can find the sum of those values by multiplying.

\[\text{mean}=\text{sum}\div\text{number of values}\]
\[\text{sum}=\text{mean}\times\text{number of values}\]
\[\text{sum}=16\times10\]
\[\text{sum}=160\]

If 7 and 13 are removed from the set of numbers, the new sum is \(160-20=140\). Find the mean of the remaining 8 numbers by dividing:

\[140\div8=17.5\]

questions.question: Points A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H are all on a straight line in that order. The distance between each pair of adjacent points is the same. If the distance between points A and H is 56, what is the distance between points B and E?

solution.exhibit_text: Because the distance between each pair of adjacent points is the same, each of the 7 segments \(\overline{AB},\overline{BC},\overline{CD},\overline{DE},\overline{EF},\overline{FG}\), and \(\overline{GH}\) has the same length. These 7 segments make up segment \(\overline{AH}\). Since the length of \(\overline{AH}\) is 56, the length of each of the 7 small segments is \(56\div7\), or 8. The distance between points B and E is the sum of the lengths of the 3 equal segments \(\overline{BC}\), \(\overline{CD}\), and \(\overline{DE}\), so the distance between points B and E is \(3\times8\), or 24.

questions.question:
If \(q\) and \(r\) are integers, in which of the following equations **must** \(q\) be positive?
Select the **two** correct answers.

solution.exhibit_text:
When you see variables in the answer choices, Picking Numbers may be a helpful strategy. Try each answer choice and see if the statement can be true with a negative \(q\). Pick a simple number for \(q\); since all of the answer choices equal 1, \(q=-1\) will work well.

(A): \((-1)\times r^2=1\). Therefore, \(r^2\) would have to equal \(-1\), which is impossible. Keep.
(B): \(-1-r=1\). Therefore, \(r=-2\). Eliminate.
(C): \(-1r=1\). Therefore, \(r=-1\). Eliminate.
(D): \((-1)^2r=1\). Therefore, \(r=1\). Eliminate.
(E): \((-1)^3\times r^2=1\). This equals \(-r^2=1\). Therefore, \(r^2\) would have to equal \(-1\), which is impossible. Keep.

All of the answer choices can work with a negative \(q\) except for (A) and (E), which are correct.

questions.question: If \(x\) and \(y\) are non-zero integers and \(x^2y<0\), which statement **must** be true?

solution.exhibit_text: Since \(x\) and \(y\) are non-zero integers and the square of any non-zero integer is positive, the expression \(x^2\) must be positive. You are told that \(x^2y<0\), or that \(x^2y\) is negative. Since the product of a positive and a negative is negative, this means that \(y\) must be negative.

questions.question: In a recent survey, 80% of the people polled were registered voters and 75% of the registered voters voted in the last election. What fraction of all those surveyed were registered voters who did **not** vote in the last election?

solution.exhibit_text: Whenever you have a percent problem that doesn't give you a definite amount and asks a question like "What fraction of the total...?" you should pick a number for the total. Since you're dealing with percents here and will be converting the percents to fractions, a good number for the total is 100. So, say that 100 people were polled. 80% of the 100 people were registered voters, so 80 people were registered voters. 75% of the registered voters voted in the last election, so \(75\%\times80\), or 60 people, voted in the last election. If 60 of the 80 registered voters actually voted in the last election, then \(80-60=20\) of the registered voters did **not** vote in the last election. The fraction of the people surveyed who were registered but did not vote is \(\dfrac{20}{100}\), or \(\dfrac{1}{5}\).

questions.question: Suppose \(R=\dfrac{a}{b}\) and \(S=\dfrac{a+1}{b+1}\), and \(a\) and \(b\) do not equal \(-1\) or \(0\). What is \(\dfrac{R}{S}\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
Substitute the values of \(R\) and \(S\) into the fraction \(\dfrac{R}{S}\) and simplify:

\[\dfrac{R}{S}=\dfrac{\tfrac{a}{b}}{\tfrac{a+1}{b+1}}\]
\[=\dfrac{a}{b}\div\dfrac{a+1}{b+1}\]
\[=\dfrac{a}{b}\times\dfrac{b+1}{a+1}\]
\[=\dfrac{a(b+1)}{b(a+1)}\]

Distribute \(a\) and \(b\) to get \(\dfrac{ab+a}{ab+b}\).

questions.question: A rectangular concrete patio is 20 feet long, 12 feet wide, and 4 inches thick. What is the volume, in cubic feet, of the concrete?

solution.exhibit_text:
First convert 4 inches to \(\tfrac{1}{3}\) foot. Then, multiply the length times the width times the depth to calculate the volume, in cubic feet:

\[20\times12\times\dfrac{1}{3}=20\times4=80\]

questions.question:
A local community center surveyed its members to determine whether they take Yoga classes, Pilates classes, both, or neither. The results were as follows:
• 42 members take Yoga.
• 36 members take Pilates.
• 14 members take both Yoga and Pilates.
• 9 members take neither class.

Use the information provided to determine how many members were surveyed and how many take only Pilates.

There were [blank1] members surveyed, and [blank2] members take only Pilates.

solution.exhibit_text: To find the number of members who take only Yoga, subtract those who take both classes from the total number of Yoga participants: \(42-14=28\). Similarly, the number of members who take only Pilates is \(36-14=22\). The total number of members surveyed is the sum of those who take only Yoga, only Pilates, both classes, and neither: \(28+22+14+9=73\). There were **73** members surveyed, and **22** members take only Pilates.

questions.question:
Two expressions are given:
\(10-x\)
\(5(3x-4)\)

Which of these are equivalent to the difference of these expressions, if the first expression is subtracted from the second expression?
Select the **three** correct answers.

solution.exhibit_text: Set up an expression that subtracts the first expression from the second expression, using parentheses to make sure you don't lose any of the signs: \(5(3x-4)-(10-x)\). Distribute the 5: \(15x-20-(10-x)\). Rewrite the terms that are in parentheses, making sure to distribute the subtraction sign before the parentheses: \(15x-20-10+x\). Then combine like terms: \(15x+x-20-10=16x-30\). This matches (E). Rearranging the terms before adding them also yields (A) and (D).
